paper.title_en: Probing the inner structure of bound states
paper.abstract_en: We show how constructing a composite particle eigenstate reveals its internal structure. Using quantum subspace expansion (QSE), we optimize states with different sets of operators and use their fidelities with the full QSE state to measure the importance of each added operator type. Taking the scalar meson of the massive Schwinger model as a benchmark, we find that fermion bilinears suffice at large fermion masses. At small masses, two classes of four-fermion operators play important but very different roles: the four fermion operators with two fermions and 2 anti-fermions at small distance give little improvement. In contrast, spatially extended meson-meson operators produce a large gain in state fidelity. Turning to observables, we find that the scalar charge is much more sensitive to the meson-meson operators than e.g. the meson mass. The parton distribution function (PDF) also changes from symmetric to asymmetric about the momentum fraction 1/2, along with the growing importance of meson-meson operators. These results establish QSE as a tool for probing the internal structure of composite particles and connecting it to observable properties.
